correctness.rationale: The graph joining ascent pairs has position-interval connected components, because each intermediate vertex connects to an endpoint; each ascent splits recursively along a point of intermediate value into cover pairs, so the cover graph has the same components. Those components exactly match unique skew-indecomposable factors. Any nonsingleton skew block of size s has a connected cover graph and at least s-1 counted upward covers, with no cross-block edges. Therefore the full skew-factor series is 1/(1-x-sum_{s>=2}x^s C_s(q)). At fixed q-degree r, only factors of sizes <=r+1 and at most r nonsingletons contribute, giving the finite coefficient formula with P_r in Z[x], degree <=2r. At x=1 only r copies of size2 q^1 factors survive, so P_r(1)=1. The coefficient expansion for n>=2r is exactly polynomial degree r leading 1/r!; C_3(q)=3q^2 determines second coefficient and eventual initial strict increase. Independently enumerated all n<=8 permutations using literal three-index cover definition, obtaining low-r counts matching displayed formulas.

value.rationale: Exact distributional information for the upward strong Bruhat cover statistic is a natural enumerative gap raised in recent boxed-mesh literature. The universal stabilization for every fixed edge degree turns finitely many skew-indecomposable blocks into explicit, reusable coefficient formulas and yields a rigorous eventually increasing initial segment; it is stronger than known initial tables and different from global unimodality.
